ibessonov Looks good to me.

ibessonov, ktkalenko@gridgain.com, Hi guys.

Could you please explain why the fileIO is not being closed now?

This leads to unable to delete these files (freeing space) until the process is complete on unix.

Hi NSAmelchev,

as far as I see, FileHandleManagerImpl.WALWriter#body does close a fileIO instance when we call walWriter.close().

Can you explain your scenario in more details? Is this a different fileIO instance?

The idea of the fix was to move all remaining fileIO manipulations to wal writer thread, thus preventing channel interruption if user thread is interrupted.

ibessonov, I have created a reproducer and a fix: PR.
Could you take a look, please?

NSAmelchev I see now, thank you!

That was clearly a mistake from my side. In your PR I would recommend hiding walWriter.close(); in else branch of mmap check.

Alternative way to fix it would be like this I believe, but now it seems more dangerous to me, we would need to look into code more carefully:

Index: modules/core/src/main/java/org/apache/ignite/internal/processors/cache/persistence/wal/filehandle/FileHandleManagerImpl.java
